A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prototype-driven curriculum for masked image modeling. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable supplementary material.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original ImageNet experiments comparing curricula, training durations, temperatures, and prototype-identification settings.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds five-shot transfer results on eight datasets in Table 3 and supplementary qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The MAE objective, clustering procedure, normalized centroid distances, temperature-controlled sampling, and effective-dataset-size scheduling remain unchanged. The supplementary material documents and analyzes the existing method.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from ImageNet to five-shot classification on CUB-200, SUN397, OxfordPets, Caltech101, UCF101, DTD, Flowers102, and Food101. This substantially broadens transfer domains and introduces evaluation with scarce labels; pretraining coverage remains ImageNet.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains standard MAE and the hard-sample curriculum adapted from Sorscher et al. The prototype-identification comparators also remain unchanged. The added transfer evaluation introduces no distinct competing algorithm.

E3.justification: The new transfer protocol trains linear classifiers with five labeled examples per class, comparing 200/400-epoch curriculum models with a 1600-epoch baseline. Separately, the temperature-table caption changes the annealing range from 0.05–0.2 to 0.07–0.6, matching Section 4.1 in both versions. This is a reported-setting correction, without evidence that the retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Supplementary Figures 6–8 add qualitative comparisons of centroid-distance ordering across SIFT, untrained, MAE, and DINO feature spaces for nine ImageNet categories. These extend the existing prototype-identification analysis; the quantitative temperature, architecture, feature-space, and cluster-count ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: New Table 3 reports means and standard deviations over three runs. This introduces uncertainty reporting for the added transfer evaluation, while the original ImageNet results retain point estimates. The PDFs do not establish increased repetition of existing experiments.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports eight-dataset average five-shot accuracies of 41.77% for the 1600-epoch baseline, 42.18% for the 200-epoch curriculum, and 47.23% for the 400-epoch curriculum. These are newly reported comparisons at different training budgets, not revisions to earlier scores. Existing ImageNet numerical results are retained, and supplementary figures add qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the sampling distribution, effective dataset size, and asymptotic limit, are unchanged. Neither version adds substantive proofs or formal theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about prototype-driven curricula improving MAE efficiency and representation quality. The transfer experiments provide additional support without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: The added few-shot discussion extends the efficiency interpretation to transfer with scarce labels. The supplement interprets its visualizations as showing more consistent organization of prototypical views in DINO spaces than in MAE or SIFT spaces. Existing limitations and future-work discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Supplementary Tables 6–7 substantially expand previously sparse downstream implementation details: 100-epoch AdamW fine-tuning, 90-epoch LARS linear probing, batch sizes, learning rates, warm-up, regularization, augmentation, and learning-rate scaling. These are newly disclosed recipes, not demonstrated changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the eight transfer datasets and removes the DATA reference by Chang et al. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to MIM, dataset selection, and importance sampling remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. Changes include a few-shot results paragraph, supplementary explanatory text, and limited caption editing. Section 4.4 retains stale references to Table 4a–c after the corresponding table becomes Table 5.

P2.justification: v2 adds the transfer-results table, two configuration tables, and three substantial multi-panel supplementary figures. It also relocates Figure 5 and rearranges the retained temperature and prototype-identification tables together on page 8. This substantially expands and reorganizes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important evidential gap in v1: evaluation was confined to ImageNet, whereas Table 3 tests transfer across eight datasets with three-run uncertainty reporting. Supplementary Tables 6–7 also fill substantial gaps in downstream reproducibility information. Together these strengthen validation and documentation of the central efficiency claim. Earlier prose/table inconsistencies persist, and table renumbering introduces stale references, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantive gains.
